```{python}
#| tags: [setup]
import sys, os
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath("."))
from _pcpkg import *  # noqa: F401,F403
import doe_report as D
import tables as T          # complex tables: merged cells, footnotes (T.<builder>(...).show())
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

DOC = "PCP-009"
UO = "virus_filtration"
UO_TITLE = "Small-Virus Retentive Filtration (Step 9)"


def g(x):
    """A number as the record has it, without trailing zeros."""
    return f"{x:g}"


def f2(x):
    return f"{x:.2f}"


# --- revision, investigation and method decision -----------------------------------------
V1_APPROVED = rev1_date(DOC)                 # Version 1.0 of this plan
V1_REPORTS = REV1["effective"]              # the date the Version 1.0 title blocks carried
INV_OPEN, INV_CLOSE, INV_CLASS = INV["opened"], INV["closed"], INV["classification"]
AMD_DATE = AMD["date"]

assert "PCP-" in _ca2 and "criteria" in _ca2 and "fragment method" in _ca2

# --- parameters: the set-points and NOR the studies were planned against -------------------

FV, FP = uo.param("filtration_volume"), uo.param("pressure")
Vol, Prs = FV.name, FP.name
vol, prs = Vol[0].lower() + Vol[1:], Prs[0].lower() + Prs[1:]
u_vol, u_prs = FV.unit, FP.unit
for _p in (FV, FP):     # no NOR or set-point of this step was changed at Version 2.0
    assert list(_p.nor) == list(_p.nor_characterized) and _p.setpoint == _p.setpoint_characterized
assert D.rsm_factors(UO) == D.screening_factors(UO) == ["filtration_volume", "pressure"]
k_fac = len(D.rsm_factors(UO))
# the load range is widened upward only, the pressure range on both sides of the NOR
assert FV.prange[0] == FV.nor[0] and FV.prange[1] > FV.nor[1]
assert FP.prange[0] < FP.nor[0] and FP.prange[1] > FP.nor[1]
# both ranges extend further above the NOR than below it
assert all((p.nor[0] - p.prange[0]) < (p.prange[1] - p.nor[1]) for p in (FV, FP))
_scope = char_scope_df().set_index("Step").loc[9]
assert _scope["Parameters"] == _scope["Multivariate"] == k_fac and _scope["Univariate"] == 0

# --- designs ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
n_scr, n_rsm = doe_runs(UO, "screening"), doe_runs(UO, "rsm")
cp_scr, cp_rsm = doe_centre_points(UO, "screening"), doe_centre_points(UO, "rsm")
pm_scr = D.planned_matrix_df(UO, "screening", coded=True)
pm_rsm = D.planned_matrix_df(UO, "rsm", coded=True)
n_fac_scr = int((pm_scr["Type"] == "factorial").sum())
n_fac_rsm = int((pm_rsm["Type"] == "factorial").sum())
n_ax_rsm = int((pm_rsm["Type"] == "axial").sum())
assert n_fac_scr == n_fac_rsm == 2 ** k_fac and n_ax_rsm == 2 * k_fac
assert n_scr == n_fac_scr + cp_scr and n_rsm == n_fac_rsm + n_ax_rsm + cp_rsm
assert set(np.abs(pm_rsm.loc[pm_rsm["Type"] == "axial", ["A", "B"]].to_numpy()).ravel()) == {0, 1}  # face-centred
p_scr = 1 + k_fac + k_fac * (k_fac - 1) // 2      # intercept, main effects, interaction
p_rsm = p_scr + k_fac                             # and one quadratic term per factor
df_pe_scr, df_pe_rsm = cp_scr - 1, cp_rsm - 1
df_lof_scr = n_scr - p_scr - df_pe_scr
df_lof_rsm = n_rsm - p_rsm - df_pe_rsm
assert df_lof_scr == 1

# --- criteria (PCMP-001 Version 2.0) --------------------------------------------------------
crit = {r: D.effective_acceptance(UO, r) for r in ("mvm_lrf", "xmulv_lrf", "lmw_cesds_pct")}
c_mvm, c_xmulv, c_frag = crit["mvm_lrf"][0], crit["xmulv_lrf"][0], crit["lmw_cesds_pct"][1]
assert crit["mvm_lrf"][2] == crit["xmulv_lrf"][2] == "lower" and crit["lmw_cesds_pct"][2] == "upper"
assert c_mvm == c_xmulv                                    # one platform claim for both viruses
assert D.effective_acceptance(UO, "step_yield") is None    # step yield has no criterion
assert D.acceptance_basis(UO, "mvm_lrf") == D.acceptance_basis(UO, "xmulv_lrf") == "platform claim"
assert D.acceptance_basis(UO, "lmw_cesds_pct") == "drug substance"
_iac = D.iac_table(UO)
assert not _iac["tightened"].any() and not _iac["widened"].any()
_frag = _iac[_iac["response"] == "lmw_cesds_pct"].iloc[0]
assert _frag["downstream_fold"] == 1 and _frag["downstream_added"] == 0   # no later step changes fragments
assert D.iac_verification(UO).empty        # no criterion relies on a platform worst case of this step
# Version 1.0: the nominal log reduction of the step less an allowance for assay variability
_r1 = D.rev1_criteria(UO).set_index("response")
r1_mvm, r1_xmulv = float(_r1.loc["mvm_lrf", "low"]), float(_r1.loc["xmulv_lrf", "low"])
_vc = csv("viral_clearance.csv").set_index("step").loc[D.VIRAL_STEP_ROW[UO]]
_allow = (float(_vc["MVM"]) - r1_mvm, float(_vc["XMuLV"]) - r1_xmulv)
assert abs(_allow[0] - _allow[1]) < 1e-9
v1_allow = _allow[0]
assert c_mvm < r1_mvm and c_xmulv < r1_xmulv                # both Version 2.0 criteria are lower
# Version 1.0 also quoted a floor: the cumulative requirement less the other steps' nominal clearance
floor_m, floor_x = D.acceptance_for(UO, "mvm_lrf")[0], D.acceptance_for(UO, "xmulv_lrf")[0]
# the modular claim: the platform claims of the steps that clear each virus (PCMP-001 §7.4)
_all = D.iac_table()
_claims = _all[_all["basis"] == "platform claim"]
_cx, _cm = _claims[_claims["response"] == "xmulv_lrf"], _claims[_claims["response"] == "mvm_lrf"]
assert set(_cx["step_key"]) == {"viral_inactivation", "aex", UO}
assert set(_cm["step_key"]) == {"aex", UO}
sum_x, req_x = float(_cx["iac_low"].sum()), float(_cx["ds_low"].iloc[0])
sum_m, req_m = float(_cm["iac_low"].sum()), float(_cm["ds_low"].iloc[0])
assert sum_x >= req_x and sum_m >= req_m
aex_m = float(_cm.loc[_cm["step_key"] == "aex", "iac_low"].iloc[0])
assert c_mvm > aex_m                                       # this step carries the larger MVM claim
_reg = cqa_reg.set_index("key")
assert _reg.loc["lrv_mvm", "set_by"] == "aex" and _reg.loc["lrv_xmulv", "set_by"] == "viral_inactivation"
assert _reg.loc["fragments_lmw", "set_by"] == "harvest"
assert _reg.loc["lrv_mvm", "criticality"] == _reg.loc["lrv_xmulv", "criticality"] == "VH"
assert _reg.loc["fragments_lmw", "criticality"] == "L"
assert cqas_for(UO).empty                                  # the step forms no quality attribute

# --- scale-down model qualification ------------------------------------------------------
_sq = csv("sdm_qualification.csv")
_sq = _sq[_sq["step"] == UO]
_outs = [c for c in _sq.columns if c not in ("study", "step", "scale", "run") and _sq[c].notna().any()]
assert _outs == ["step_yield"]                             # the qualification compares step yield
for _r in crit:
    assert D.sdm_offset(UO, _r) is None                    # no offset for an output with a criterion
_off = D.sdm_offset(UO, "step_yield")

# --- studies: execution windows and the fragment method -----------------------------------

    assert csv(f"doe_{UO}_{_k}.csv")["lmw_sec_pct"].isna().all()

# --- statistics ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

pi_pct = g(round(100 * D.PI_LEVEL, 6))
lo_pct, hi_pct = g(round(100 * (1 - D.PI_LEVEL) / 2, 6)), g(round(100 * (1 + D.PI_LEVEL) / 2, 6))
```

# Purpose and scope {#sec-purpose}

The A-Mab drug substance process is being transferred from the development site in `{python} SENDING_LOCATION`, to the commercial drug substance site in `{python} RECEIVING_LOCATION`, under the Process Transfer Plan PTP-001. Stage 1 process characterization supports that transfer [@fda2011]. It establishes which process parameters affect product quality, and it defines the ranges within which the commercial process may be operated. This plan covers Step 9 of the drug substance train, small-virus retentive filtration. The commercial process runs at a production bioreactor scale of `{python} f"{V['commercial_scale_l']:,}"` L.

The step is the dedicated small-virus removal step of the purification train and the principal clearance step for minute virus of mice (MVM), a parvovirus. It removes virus by size. Its clearance is therefore orthogonal to that of low-pH viral inactivation (Step 6), which inactivates enveloped virus, and to that of anion exchange chromatography (Step 8), which binds virus to the resin [@ichq5a].

The study covers both process parameters of the step, `{python} vol` and `{python} prs`. It measures the log reduction factor (LRF) of MVM and of xenotropic murine leukemia virus (XMuLV), the level of fragments and the step yield. It is run in a scale-down model, on load representative of the anion exchange pool that feeds the step at commercial scale.

The qualification of the membrane itself is held by the filter manufacturer and is not repeated here. The cumulative viral clearance claim of the drug substance is consolidated in the master report PCMR-001 across the steps that clear virus, and this study establishes the contribution of Step 9 only. Process validation at commercial scale is covered by the validation programme and not by this study.

The studies of this step ran under Version 1.0 of this plan, from `{python} first_start` to `{python} last_end`. Version 2.0 is an amendment issued after them. It restates the protocol of Version 1.0 with the changes listed in @sec-changes, and its criteria govern the analysis that the report PCR-009 Version 2.0 presents. The deliverable of the study is PCR-009.

## Changes in this revision {#sec-changes}

Version 1.0 of this plan was approved on `{python} V1_APPROVED`, before the first study of the step began on `{python} first_start`. Version 2.0 replaces it and is issued under the investigation INV-001. Quality Assurance opened INV-001 on `{python} INV_OPEN` after its review of the master report PCMR-001 Version 1.0 for readiness of the Biologics License Application, and closed it on `{python} INV_CLOSE` with the classification `{python} INV_CLASS`. INV-001 found that the criteria used to judge each step in the proven acceptable range (PAR) analysis had been set after the data were seen and were in no approved protocol (finding 1). Its corrective action CA2 amends each step plan with the criteria and the fragment method of the master plan PCMP-001 Version 2.0. The design, the sampling, the spiking and the decision rules of Version 1.0 are kept where the changes below do not replace them. This revision makes the following changes.

1. Acceptance criteria. Each output with a criterion is judged against the intermediate acceptance criterion (IAC) that PCMP-001 §7.3 and §7.4 derive for it (@tbl-criteria-change). The MVM LRF and the XMuLV LRF are each held to the platform claim of this step, `{python} f2(c_mvm)` log10. Version 1.0 judged them against the nominal log reduction of the step less `{python} f2(v1_allow)` log10 for assay variability, which gave `{python} f2(r1_mvm)` for MVM and `{python} f2(r1_xmulv)` for XMuLV. Both Version 2.0 criteria are lower than these limits. Version 1.0 also quoted a floor for each virus, the cumulative requirement less the nominal clearance of the other steps (`{python} f2(floor_m)` for MVM and `{python} f2(floor_x)` for XMuLV), to show the margin of the cumulative claim. PCMP-001 §7.4 replaces the floor with a check that the platform claims of the steps sum to the cumulative requirement (@sec-criteria). Fragments are added as an output, with the drug substance criterion of ≤ `{python} f2(c_frag)` %, because no step after this one changes them.
2. Fragment method. Fragments are measured by non-reduced capillary electrophoresis with sodium dodecyl sulfate (nrCE-SDS). This method was set for every study at every step from `{python} AMD_DATE` by the analytical method decision AMD-001 (PCMP-001 §7.8). Version 1.0 did not assess fragments at this step. Both designs of the step started after that date, and fragments were measured by nrCE-SDS on every run (@tbl-methods-by-study). No fragment result by size exclusion chromatography exists at this step.
3. Scale-down model. The model is qualified by its offset from manufacturing scale (PCMP-001 §7.1), and no longer by the Version 1.0 test of no statistically significant difference between the scales. The qualification runs, and the estimate of the offsets, come before the first screening run. The decision whether the model is qualified for an output is made at analysis. The outputs that the qualification compares carry no criterion at this step, so their offsets are recorded and no conclusion depends on them. The two LRF and fragments are not compared at both scales, and @sec-sdm states the assumptions on which their judgement rests.
4. Model adequacy. A response-surface model sets a range only if it meets the adequacy criteria of PCMP-001 §7.2 (@sec-criteria). Version 1.0 judged lack of fit, the residuals and the residual standard error. The model F-test and the limit on the gap between R² and predicted R² are added. So are two tests that every step plan applies in the same way. The residuals are regressed on the predicted value and on run order, and Cook's distance measures the influence of each run.
5. Judgement statistics. The two LRF are judged at the worst case within the normal operating range (NOR). That is the mean predicted LRF at the least favourable combination of NOR low, set-point and NOR high of the other parameter (PCMP-001 §6.4). Fragments are judged on the `{python} pi_pct` % prediction interval of a single batch, which now includes the uncertainty of the fitted coefficients. Version 1.0 judged every output on the prediction interval of a single batch.
6. Verification of platform worst cases. PCMP-001 §7.5 lets a report replace a platform worst case, on which the criteria upstream of its step rely, with an A-Mab prediction bound. No criterion relies on a platform worst case of this step, so PCR-009 has none to verify. No criterion of this step was tightened or widened by the verification at other steps (@tbl-iac).
7. Execution windows. The record now gives the execution window of each study of the step (@tbl-windows), which the Version 1.0 records did not (INV-001 finding 5). The Version 1.0 title block carried `{python} V1_REPORTS`, the date on which the Version 1.0 reports were approved, in place of the date on which this plan was approved. The revision history gives the approval date.

# Objectives {#sec-objectives}

The study has the following objectives.

1. Qualify the scale-down model of the step under the offset rule of the master plan PCMP-001 (§7.1). The qualification runs and the offset estimates come before the first screening run, and the decision for each output is made at analysis.
2. Determine which of the parameters in @tbl-params affect the MVM LRF, the XMuLV LRF, fragments and step yield, in which direction and by how much.
3. Fit a response-surface model for each output over the ranges studied, and test whether it meets the adequacy criteria in @sec-criteria.
4. Derive a proven acceptable range for each parameter against each output with a criterion, which are the two LRF and fragments, by the method in @sec-par.
5. Classify each parameter under the parameter classification procedure SOP-4001, and state what the step contributes to the control strategy and to the modular viral clearance claim.

The screening design identifies the parameters that have an effect. The response-surface model is the predictive model, and every range claimed in the report PCR-009 will be derived from it.

# Prior knowledge and quality risk basis {#sec-prior}

## Unit-operation description and prior knowledge {#sec-uo}

Virus filtration removes virus by size. The membrane has a distribution of pore sizes chosen to retain the smallest viruses of concern, the parvoviruses, while the antibody passes through. Retention is by sieving. It therefore depends on the integrity of the pore structure and on how the effective pore size changes as the membrane fouls during the batch.

MVM is close to the cut-off of the pore size distribution. Its retention depends on the fraction of pores at the large end of the distribution and on the flow through them. As product and residual impurity foul the membrane, the flow redistributes toward the least fouled pores, which are the largest, and small virus can pass. MVM retention is therefore expected to fall as the volume filtered per unit area rises. A low transmembrane pressure, or an interruption of flow, can also let virus held in the pore structure diffuse through the membrane. For this reason pressure is controlled as well as volume.

XMuLV is many times larger than the pores. It is expected to be retained completely while the membrane is intact, and its clearance to be insensitive to the operating parameters. The post-use integrity test under the operation procedure SOP-2012 confirms that the membrane was intact.

The antibody is small enough to pass the pores freely. Step yield is limited only by the product held up in the fouled membrane and in the system, and it is expected to be high. Fragments are smaller than the intact antibody and pass the pores in the same way. The step is therefore not expected to change the fragment level of its load.

The step is a platform operation. It was used for the three earlier platform antibodies, X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab, and for A-Mab clinical supply [@amab2009]. The mechanism of removal is sieving and does not depend on the antibody. Platform experience therefore supports the ranges chosen in @sec-factors and the expectation that MVM retention falls with load while XMuLV retention does not. The platform history also gives the claim of this step, a log reduction of `{python} f2(c_mvm)` log10 for each model virus (master plan PCMP-001 §7.4).

Prior knowledge does not replace the study. The load of this step is the anion exchange pool of the A-Mab process, and how that pool fouls the membrane depends on the product and on the residual impurities it carries. The maximum load and the pressure range are therefore established on A-Mab material.

## Quality attributes in scope {#sec-cqa}

The step forms no quality attribute. It contributes log reduction to the two viral safety attributes, and its output is judged against the criterion for fragments (@tbl-cqa).

```{python}
#| output: asis
_cq = cqas_by_keys(["lrv_mvm", "lrv_xmulv", "fragments_lmw"])
T.frame(_cq[["Category", "CQA", "Acceptance", "Criticality", "Tool #1"]],
        "Quality attributes to which the step contributes, with their drug substance criteria and "
        "criticality.", "tbl-cqa", merge=["Category"],
        align=["P{2.4cm}", "P{4.6cm}", "P{3.6cm}", "l", "r"],
        notes=[("", "VH, very high. L, low. Tool #1 is the criticality score of the A-Mab case "
                    "study, the product of impact and uncertainty.")]).show()
```

Both viral clearance attributes have very high criticality. It was assigned by rule, because a viral contamination would directly harm the patient (master plan PCMP-001 §3). Each requirement is cumulative over the train and is met by the sum of the claims of several steps (PCMP-001 §7.4). The register assigns MVM clearance to anion exchange and XMuLV clearance to low-pH viral inactivation. Low-pH viral inactivation makes no claim for MVM, because a parvovirus has no lipid envelope for low pH to disrupt. The MVM requirement therefore rests on anion exchange and on this step alone, and this step carries the larger of the two MVM claims (@sec-criteria).

Fragments have low criticality. They are formed in culture and during the harvest hold, by proteases released from lysed cells, and the register assigns them to harvest (PCMP-001 §3). No step after this one changes fragments, so the output of this step carries the drug substance criterion for them (@sec-criteria).

Step yield is a process performance output. No drug substance attribute maps to it, so it is measured and reported but judged against no criterion.

## Risk-based prioritization of parameters {#sec-risk}

The risk assessment RA-001 ranked every process parameter of the train on its potential impact on the quality attributes and on its potential to interact with other parameters [@ichq9]. Parameters ranked high, or with a likely interaction, were assigned to multivariate study. Parameters whose range could be supported one factor at a time were assigned to univariate study (master plan PCMP-001 §4). Both parameters of this step were assigned to multivariate study, and none to univariate study.

The `{python} vol` sets how far fouling has progressed by the end of the batch, and with it the share of the flow that passes the largest pores. It is therefore expected to bound the MVM claim. The `{python} prs` sets the flux. A low pressure lets virus held in the pore structure diffuse through, and a high pressure compresses the fouling layer and raises the flux through the pores that remain open. Both parameters act on the same population of large pores. The effect of one may therefore depend on the level of the other, and both designs estimate the interaction of the two.

The other operating variables of the step are held at their set-points under the operation procedure SOP-2012 and rest on platform experience (@sec-univariate).

# Materials and methods {#sec-methods}

## Scale-down model and its qualification {#sec-sdm}

The study will be run on a laboratory-scale filtration system fitted with the same membrane type and membrane chemistry as the commercial step. The model is scaled on membrane area, so that the volumetric load in `{python} u_vol`, the transmembrane pressure and the flux per unit area are the same as at commercial scale. The `{python} prs` is the transmembrane pressure across the filter. The load is matched because the product and the residual impurity it carries are what foul the membrane, and a cleaner pool fouls it more slowly. The filtration temperature is matched because a higher temperature lowers the viscosity of the pool and raises the flux at a given pressure. The hold-up volume per unit area is matched because it fixes how much product is left in the membrane and the tubing at the end of a run, which limits step yield.

The qualification study `{python} ID_SDM` follows the scale-down model procedure SOP-1001. The scale-down system will be run `{python} n_sd` times at the set-points of @tbl-params on representative anion exchange pool. The flux decay profile, the step yield and the post-use integrity test result will be compared with the records of `{python} n_m` manufacturing-scale batches.

Under the offset rule of the master plan PCMP-001 (§7.1), the offset of an output is the mean of the scale-down runs at set-point minus the mean of the manufacturing-scale batches. It is reported with its two-sided `{python} off_ci` % confidence interval, each end of which is a one-sided `{python} off_one` % confidence bound. The model is qualified for an output when the conclusion against its criterion over the NOR is the same with the offset at either end of that interval. An output with no criterion at the step has its offset recorded only. Step yield and flux decay have no criterion at this step, so their offsets are recorded and no conclusion depends on them (@tbl-sdm).

The qualification runs will be made, and the offsets estimated, before the first screening run. The decision whether the model is qualified for an output is made at analysis, because it needs the response-surface model of the step. At this step that decision applies to no output with a criterion, because none is compared at both scales.

The two LRF and fragments are not compared at both scales. Their offset is unknown, not zero, and they are judged as the scale-down model predicts them (PCMP-001 §7.1). Two assumptions then carry the judgement, and the report PCR-009 will state each where it is used.

- Virus cannot be spiked into a manufacturing batch, so every log reduction claimed for this step comes from the scale-down model [@ichq5a]. Its representativeness rests on the design of the spiking model described above. The model uses the same membrane at the same volumetric load, pressure and flux per unit area, with matched load, temperature and hold-up.
- The fragment result rests on the mechanism of the step. The clipped species are smaller than the intact antibody, so they pass the pores as freely as the antibody does, at either scale. The step is therefore not expected to change the fragment level of its load, and a scale-down result is taken to represent the manufacturing step.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_sdm = pd.DataFrame([
    [_lab["mvm_lrf"], T.crit(*crit["mvm_lrf"]), "No",
     "Scale-down prediction, no offset. Rests on the spiking model."],
    [_lab["xmulv_lrf"], T.crit(*crit["xmulv_lrf"]), "No",
     "Scale-down prediction, no offset. Rests on the spiking model."],
    ["Fragments (LMW, %, nrCE-SDS)", T.crit(*crit["lmw_cesds_pct"]), "No",
     "Scale-down prediction, no offset. Rests on the mechanism of the step."],
    [_lab["step_yield"], "None", f"Yes, {n_sd} scale-down runs and {n_m} manufacturing batches",
     "Offset recorded. No conclusion depends on it."],
    ["Flux decay at the end of the load", "None", "Yes, in the same runs and batches",
     "Offset recorded. No conclusion depends on it."],
], columns=["Output", "Criterion", "Compared at both scales", "Judgement at manufacturing scale"])
T.frame(_sdm, "Outputs of the step and how each is carried to manufacturing scale.", "tbl-sdm",
        align=["P{3.0cm}", "l", "P{4.8cm}", "P{5.2cm}"]).show()
```

The qualification will be repeated if the membrane type, the filtration temperature or the composition of the load material changes. PCR-009 will state the qualification result before it reports any log reduction.

## Operation {#sec-operation}

The load is the flow-through pool of the anion exchange step. Each run will be operated at constant transmembrane pressure up to the volumetric load set by its design point, and the filtrate will be collected in fractions across the load.

Before each run the filter will be wetted and its integrity tested. After each run the post-use integrity test will be performed. Both tests follow the operation procedure SOP-2012. A run whose post-use integrity test fails will be excluded from the analysis and recorded as a deviation. A failed test means that the membrane was not intact, and the log reduction measured across it then says nothing about the step.

Each design point will be executed once, with both model viruses spiked into the load before filtration. Step yield will be determined from the same run by protein mass balance, from the ultraviolet absorbance of the load and of the pooled filtrate. The filtrate pool of each run will also be tested for fragments. Runs will be executed in random order within each design.

Filtration will be continuous. The claim made from this study applies to uninterrupted operation, because an interruption of flow allows virus held in the pore structure to diffuse through it. An interruption at commercial scale is a deviation and lies outside the operating region this study defines.

## Analytical methods {#sec-analytical}

@tbl-assays gives the method and the method validation for each output that is judged against a criterion. MVM will be titrated by the median tissue culture infective dose (TCID50) assay with confirmation by quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR), and XMuLV by the TCID50 assay. Fragments will be measured by nrCE-SDS as the percentage of low molecular weight species (LMW). Step yield is calculated from the protein concentration of the load and of the filtrate pool, measured by ultraviolet absorbance.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_as = pd.DataFrame([
    [_lab["mvm_lrf"], "Infectivity titre by TCID50, with qPCR confirmation", _amv["MVM"]],
    [_lab["xmulv_lrf"], "Infectivity titre by TCID50", _amv["XMuLV"]],
    ["Fragments (LMW, %, nrCE-SDS)", "Purity by nrCE-SDS, LMW as a percentage of the total",
     _amv["Purity"]],
], columns=["Output", "Method", "Method validation"])
T.frame(_as, "Analytical methods for the outputs judged against a criterion.", "tbl-assays",
        align=["P{3.6cm}", "P{7.0cm}", "l"]).show()
```

The LRF of a run is the base ten logarithm of the total virus in the spiked load divided by the total virus in the filtrate, with both totals taken over the volume actually filtered. Cytotoxicity and interference controls will be run for the load matrix and for the filtrate matrix, and a spike recovery control will be run for each virus stock [@ichq5a].

Where no virus is detected in the filtrate, the titre will be reported at the limit of detection of the assay, and the LRF will be reported as a lower bound, not as a point value. The infectivity assays carry their own variability. The criteria are the platform claims of the step and carry no allowance for it (@sec-criteria).

Fragments are judged on nrCE-SDS results only (master plan PCMP-001 §7.8). Every run of both designs has an nrCE-SDS result for fragments, and aggregate was not measured in the designs at this step (@tbl-methods-by-study).

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.methods_by_study(["virus_filtration"]).show()
```

## Sampling plan {#sec-sampling}

Samples will be taken from the load before spiking, from the spiked load and from the filtrate (@tbl-sampling). The filtrate will be sampled as sequential fractions across the volumetric load and as a pool at the end of the run. The fractions allow the LRF to be resolved against the volume filtered within a single run, which is the variable that degrades MVM retention as the membrane fouls.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_sp = pd.DataFrame([
    ["Load", "Before spiking", "Protein concentration"],
    ["Spiked load", "After spiking, before filtration", "MVM and XMuLV titre"],
    ["Filtrate fractions", "In sequence across the volumetric load", "MVM and XMuLV titre"],
    ["Filtrate pool", "At the end of the run",
     "MVM and XMuLV titre, protein concentration, fragments by nrCE-SDS"],
], columns=["Sample", "Point of sampling", "Tested for"])
T.frame(_sp, "Samples taken in each filtration run.", "tbl-sampling",
        align=["P{3.0cm}", "P{5.0cm}", "P{6.0cm}"]).show()
```

Every sample will be identified by run number and by the volumetric load at which it was taken, and the identity will be recorded at the time of sampling. Samples may be held frozen before assay where the method validation supports it.

## Statistical methods {#sec-stats}

Both factors will be coded to the interval from −1 to +1 across the ranges studied in @tbl-params, so that the estimated effects are comparable between the two factors and between the two designs. Effects will be reported as the change in the response over half the range studied.

The screening design will be analysed with a model of both main effects and their interaction. The response-surface design will be analysed with the full quadratic model in both factors [@montgomery2017]. Coefficients will be reported with their standard errors and p-values, and effects significant at α = `{python} g(a_eff)` will be treated as real. The screening model identifies effects. The response-surface model is the predictive model, and every prediction and every range in the report PCR-009 comes from it (master plan PCMP-001 §6.2).

Each fitted response-surface model will be reported with R², adjusted R² and predicted R², the model F-test, and the test for lack of fit against the pure error from the centre points. The residuals will be plotted against the predicted value, against run order and on a normal quantile plot. They will also be regressed on the predicted value and on run order, and Cook's distance will be computed for each run. @sec-criteria gives the criteria these statistics are judged against. The centre-point replicates also give the reproducibility of each response, which will be reported as a coefficient of variation and used as the pure error term.

Fragments are judged against their criterion on the prediction interval of a single batch, because the criterion applies to each batch. The response-surface model predicts the mean response, so an interval is needed to judge a single batch. The interval comes from a Monte Carlo simulation of the fitted model and includes the model residual and the uncertainty of the fitted coefficients (@sec-par). The two LRF are judged on the mean predicted LRF at the least favourable combination of NOR low, set-point and NOR high of the other parameter, because viral clearance is validated at worst-case conditions (PCMP-001 §6.4).

Every judgement against a criterion is stated at manufacturing scale (PCMP-001 §7.1). At this step no output with a criterion has an offset. The scale-down prediction is therefore compared with the criterion without a correction, on the assumptions stated in @sec-sdm.

The analyses will be performed under the design of experiments procedure SOP-1002. They will be run from a script under version control with a fixed random seed, so that every number in PCR-009 can be regenerated from the raw data.

# Study design {#sec-design}

## Factors, ranges and study type {#sec-factors}

@tbl-params lists the parameters of the step with their set-points, the ranges studied and the NOR. These are the set-points and the NOR that the studies were planned against, and neither was changed at Version 2.0.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_pp = plan_params(UO).copy()
_pp["Set-point"] = _pp["Set-point"].map(g)
T.frame(_pp, "Parameters of the step, ranges studied and normal operating ranges.", "tbl-params",
        align=["P{4.4cm}", "l", "r", "l", "l", "l"]).show()
```

Both parameters are factors of the two designs. The range studied for `{python} vol` runs from the lower NOR edge, `{python} g(FV.prange[0])` `{python} u_vol`, to `{python} g(FV.prange[1])` `{python} u_vol`, above the upper NOR edge of `{python} g(FV.nor[1])` `{python} u_vol`. It was widened upward only, because MVM retention is expected to fall as the load rises and to hold steady at low load. The edge of acceptable performance is therefore expected above the NOR, and runs below the NOR would add little.

The range studied for `{python} prs`, from `{python} g(FP.prange[0])` to `{python} g(FP.prange[1])` `{python} u_prs`, extends beyond the NOR of `{python} g(FP.nor[0])` to `{python} g(FP.nor[1])` `{python} u_prs` at both ends. Low pressures are included because a low pressure lets retained virus diffuse through the pore structure. High pressures are included because a higher pressure compresses the fouling layer and raises the flux through the pores that remain open. Both ends can be reached by the commercial equipment, so the range also supports the assessment of a deviation.

@fig-design shows the planned design points over the ranges studied, with the NOR and the set-point. The NOR lies toward the low end of both ranges, because both ranges extend further above the NOR than below it.

## Screening design {#sec-screening}

The screening design of study `{python} ID_SCR` is a two-level full factorial in both factors with replicated centre points, `{python} n_scr` runs in total. Of these, `{python} n_fac_scr` runs are the factorial points at the corners of the ranges studied and `{python} cp_scr` are replicates of the centre point.

Because the design has only `{python} k_fac` factors, the full factorial is run, and both main effects and their interaction are estimated free of aliasing. The centre points detect curvature but cannot attribute it to a factor, and curvature is resolved at the response-surface stage. The interaction model leaves `{python} df_lof_scr` degree of freedom for lack of fit, so its fit statistics overstate how well it fits (master plan PCMP-001 §6.2). The screening runs establish the size and direction of the effects, and the reproducibility of the assays at the centre point, before the response-surface runs are made. Appendix A gives the planned coded and natural settings.

## Response-surface design {#sec-rsm}

The response-surface design of study `{python} ID_RSM` is a face-centred central composite design in both factors, `{python} n_rsm` runs in total [@montgomery2017]. It is made up of `{python} n_fac_rsm` factorial points, `{python} n_ax_rsm` axial points and `{python} cp_rsm` replicates of the centre point.

The axial points sit on the edges of the ranges studied and not beyond them. A rotatable design would place them outside those edges, at settings beyond the ranges studied, for which the step may not be claimed. The face-centred form is therefore used. The design supports the full quadratic model, which allows the response to curve against the load. The response may curve there because fouling, and with it the share of the flow through the largest pores, need not grow in proportion to the volume filtered. A model limited to straight lines would then misjudge retention at the top of the range, where the claim is decided.

The replicated centre point gives the pure error for the lack-of-fit test, with `{python} df_pe_rsm` degrees of freedom against `{python} df_lof_rsm` for lack of fit. It also gives an estimate of the reproducibility between runs that does not depend on the model. Appendix B gives the planned coded and natural settings.

## Univariate assessment {#sec-univariate}

No parameter of this step is assigned to univariate study. Both parameters in @tbl-params are factors of the two designs, and the other operating variables of the step are held at their set-points under the operation procedure SOP-2012 and rest on platform experience.

Where the study finds an effect that the two designs cannot separate, a univariate confirmation run may be added. Any such run will be justified against the data that prompted it, and the report PCR-009 will present it against the same criteria as the designed runs.

# Acceptance and decision criteria {#sec-criteria}

Criteria apply to the scale-down model, to the fitted models, to the outputs, to the ranges and classes that follow from them, and to the study as a whole.

The rule for the scale-down model is stated in @sec-sdm. The screening runs will not begin until the qualification runs are complete and the offsets are estimated. Whether the model is qualified for an output is decided at analysis.

A response-surface model is adequate for prediction when all of the following hold.

1. The model F-test is significant at α = `{python} g(a_eff)`, the level set for model terms.
2. Lack of fit against the pure error from the centre points is not significant at α = `{python} g(a_lof)`.
3. Predicted R² falls short of R² by no more than `{python} f2(gap)`. This is a limit on overfitting, because a model that fits its own runs much better than it predicts left-out runs has more terms than the data support.
4. The residuals show no pattern against the predicted value or against run order, and no single run dominates the fit. A pattern is tested by a regression of the residuals on the predicted value and on run order, and a slope significant at α = `{python} g(a_eff)` counts as a pattern. A run whose Cook's distance exceeds 4/n, where n is the number of runs, is taken to dominate the fit. The cut-off 4/n is a common convention, and it falls as the number of runs grows.
5. The normal quantile plot of the residuals shows no material departure from normality.
6. The residual standard error is small against the distance between the predicted response and its criterion.

Conditions 1 to 4 are those of the master plan PCMP-001 (§7.2), with the tests on the residuals and on influence that every step plan applies in the same way. Conditions 5 and 6 are specific to this plan.

A model that fails any condition is not used to set a range. A model that fails the lack-of-fit test or the limit on overfitting may first be refitted with a justified change of terms or transformation (PCMP-001 §7.2). Where no adequate model results, the report PCR-009 will present the response descriptively, against its criterion, over the runs of the designs, and no range will be claimed from it.

@tbl-iac gives the criterion for each output of the step and its derivation from the drug substance criterion (PCMP-001 §7.3). The two LRF are each held to the platform claim of the step, `{python} f2(c_mvm)` log10. The claim is the log reduction that the step delivered on the platform with X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab (PCMP-001 §7.4). For each virus, the claims of the steps that clear it are summed and checked against the cumulative requirement of the drug substance. For XMuLV the claims of low-pH viral inactivation, anion exchange and this step sum to `{python} f2(sum_x)` log10 against a requirement of `{python} g(req_x)`. For MVM the claims of anion exchange and this step sum to `{python} f2(sum_m)` against `{python} g(req_m)`. Of that sum, this step claims `{python} f2(c_mvm)` and anion exchange `{python} f2(aex_m)`. Each step is judged against its own claim, so a shortfall at this step is not made up by another step.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.iac_derivation(["virus_filtration"]).show()
```

Fragments carry the drug substance criterion, ≤ `{python} f2(c_frag)` %, because no step after this one changes them. They are judged on nrCE-SDS results only. Step yield has no criterion. The criteria were issued after the studies of this step had run. Their derivation uses no result of these studies, because the platform claims come from the platform history and the fragment criterion is the drug substance criterion (PCMP-001 §7.3). No criterion relies on a platform worst case of this step, so PCR-009 has none to verify (PCMP-001 §7.5).

An operating range for a parameter will be declared where the response-surface model predicts that the two LRF and fragments meet their criteria across that range. A parameter with a proven acceptable range for each of these outputs carries the intersection of the ranges into the control strategy (PCMP-001 §7.6). The design space of the step is the part of the region studied where the two LRF and fragments meet their criteria at the same time. PCR-009 will report its size from the fitted models and will not assert that it is the whole region studied.

Each parameter will be classified under the parameter classification procedure SOP-4001 from the outcome of the study, by the rules of PCMP-001 §7.7 [@amab2009]. A parameter with a significant and practically relevant effect on a critical quality attribute is classified as a critical process parameter (CPP) where its risk of falling outside its acceptable range in operation is high. It is classified as a well-controlled critical process parameter (WC-CPP) where that risk is low, because it is readily controlled and its PAR is wide against its NOR. A parameter that affects process performance but no quality attribute is classified as a key process parameter (KPP), and a parameter with neither effect as a general process parameter (GPP) [@ichq8]. Neither PCMP-001 nor SOP-4001 gives a number for a practically relevant effect or for a wide PAR. PCR-009 will therefore state the size of each effect across its PAR beside its significance, and the margin between each PAR and the NOR, and it will give the reason for each class from them.

The study will be considered successful where the scale-down model is qualified, both LRF models meet the adequacy criteria, and a proven acceptable range containing the NOR is established for each parameter against each of the two LRF. Where no such range exists, PCR-009 will report the range that does exist and the operating limit that follows from it.

# Proven acceptable ranges (planned analysis) {#sec-par}

A proven acceptable range is the range of a parameter over which an output meets its criterion, given a stated treatment of the other parameter [@ichq8]. It is derived for each parameter and for each output with a criterion in @tbl-iac, which are the two LRF and fragments. Two analyses will be run for each parameter and output, and both will be reported.

1. The set-point analysis holds the other parameter at its set-point and scans the parameter of interest across its range studied on a grid of `{python} D.PAR_GRID_SETPOINT` points, using the fitted response-surface model. Its range is the contiguous interval around the set-point over which the mean prediction meets the criterion. It shows what the parameter may do while the rest of the step is operated at target.
2. The NOR-propagated analysis scans the parameter of interest across its range studied on a grid of `{python} D.PAR_GRID` points. At each point the other parameter is set in one of two ways, which depend on the output.

For fragments, the analysis draws `{python} mc_n` values of the other parameter at each grid point. Each value comes from a normal distribution centred on the set-point, with a standard deviation of the NOR width divided by `{python} nor_sd`, and is clipped to the range studied. This assumes that the NOR spans ±`{python} nor_half` standard deviations of the routine variation of the parameter. Each draw carries the model residual and the uncertainty of the fitted coefficients. The `{python} pi_pct` % prediction interval of a single batch runs from the `{python} lo_pct`th to the `{python} hi_pct`th percentile of the simulated batches, and its upper end must not exceed the criterion.

For the two LRF, the other parameter is set at each grid point to its NOR low, its set-point and its NOR high. The lowest of the three mean predicted LRF must meet the claim of the step. Viral clearance is validated at worst-case conditions, so a claim that held only on average over the NOR would not support a validated log reduction (master plan PCMP-001 §6.4).

The NOR-propagated range is the one that supports a claim. Where the two analyses disagree, the range from the NOR-propagated analysis is carried into the control strategy, because the commercial process holds each parameter somewhere within its NOR and not at its set-point. The NOR-propagated range is therefore in general the narrower of the two.

The reported range in each case is the contiguous interval that contains the set-point. Where the prediction leaves the criterion inside the range studied, the PAR is narrower than the range studied, and the report PCR-009 will state the value at which the output crosses its criterion. A PAR that reaches the edge of the range studied is reported as reaching it, and no claim is made beyond it. Where an output does not meet its criterion even at the set-point, PCR-009 will report that no PAR exists for that output and will state the consequence for the NOR (PCMP-001 §7.6). Ranges are derived only from a model that meets the adequacy criteria in @sec-criteria.

Each PAR will be reported with a plot of the output against the parameter, with the criterion drawn, the acceptable region shaded green, and the set-point and the NOR marked. The two analyses will form the two panels of one figure, so that the cost of the NOR-propagated analysis is visible. The ranges themselves will be reported in PCR-009.

# Data management and integrity {#sec-data}

Raw data will be recorded at the time of the activity, in the electronic laboratory notebook for the filtration runs and in the laboratory information management system for the analytical results. Records will meet the ALCOA+ expectations, and the audit trails of both systems will be retained for the life of the application.

Analytical results will be transferred to the analysis by controlled file export. The fitted models, the tables and the figures of the report PCR-009 will be generated from the exported data by a single reproducible run of the analysis script. A second reviewer will confirm that the reported numbers come from that run. Any manual entry of a value into the analysis is a data integrity finding and will be handled as one.

Each study record carries its execution window (@tbl-windows). The record of any instrumented system that a study uses carries its calibration status at execution (master plan PCMP-001 §5). The studies of this step used none of the instrumented systems under calibration and change control that PCMP-001 lists.

Deviations from this plan will be recorded when they occur, and PCR-009 will present each with its assessed impact on the study. A deviation that invalidates a design point will be dispositioned before the affected runs are analysed. Where the disposition is to repeat the affected runs, the superseded data will be retained and referenced, not deleted.

# Deliverables and schedule {#sec-schedule}

The deliverable of the study is the report PCR-009. It will report the qualification of the scale-down model with the offsets of the step, the screening effects, the response-surface models with their diagnostics, the proven acceptable ranges, the design space of the step, the parameter classification, and the contribution of the step to the control strategy and to the modular viral clearance claim. It will judge the two LRF and fragments against the criteria in @tbl-iac.

The study is executed in four phases, in this order.

1. The qualification runs of the scale-down model and the estimate of the offsets (@sec-sdm).
2. The screening runs and their analysis.
3. The response-surface runs and their analysis, with the decision whether the scale-down model is qualified for each output.
4. The proven acceptable range analysis, the classification and the report.

Each phase begins when the preceding phase has met its criterion in @sec-criteria. For the first phase that criterion is the completion of the qualification runs and of the offset estimates, because the decision whether the model is qualified is made at analysis (master plan PCMP-001 §7.1). No calendar dates were fixed in advance. The studies ran in the windows of @tbl-windows. A window runs from the first to the last day of runs of its study. The studies ran one after the other, and all of them closed before the Version 1.0 reports were approved on `{python} V1_REPORTS`.

The study is scheduled against the transfer programme in the Process Transfer Plan PTP-001. Its report rolls up into the master report PCMR-001 with the reports of the other steps that clear virus.

# Risks and assumptions {#sec-risks}

The log reductions claimed for this step rest entirely on the scale-down model, because virus cannot be spiked at manufacturing scale. No output with a criterion is compared at both scales, so the claim rests on the design of the model (@sec-sdm). If the model has to be changed, it will be re-scaled on membrane area and on hold-up volume, the qualification runs will be repeated, and the change will be recorded in the report PCR-009.

Spiking adds material to the load, and retention depends on how the membrane fouls. A spike that fouled the membrane differently from unspiked process material would bias the measured log reduction. The bias would be largest at the top of the volumetric range, which is the part of the range that the claim depends on. The virus stock will therefore be clarified before addition and its volume kept small against the load volume. The flux decay of the spiked runs will be compared with that of the unspiked qualification runs.

The log reduction that can be measured is bounded by the titre of the spiked load and by the limit of detection of the infectivity assay. Where no virus is detected in the filtrate, the result is a lower bound, and a lower bound that falls short of the criterion cannot be resolved by repeating the assay. The load will therefore be spiked to a titre that allows the criterion to be demonstrated with margin, and the achieved titre will be reported with each run.

The study assumes that the anion exchange pool used in the runs represents commercial material. Anion exchange is the step immediately upstream, and its own characterization is reported in the anion exchange report PCR-008. Pool from a run that was itself out of trend will not be used, and the load material of each filtration run will be identified in PCR-009.

The judgement of fragments assumes that the step changes the fragment level of its load at neither scale, which follows from the mechanism of the step (@sec-uo). PCR-009 will state this assumption where fragments are judged.

The study assumes uninterrupted filtration, as stated in @sec-operation. The ranges it produces do not cover an interruption of flow. An interruption at commercial scale will be assessed as a deviation against the mechanism in @sec-uo, not against these ranges.

Material supply is the principal risk to the schedule. Each design point consumes anion exchange pool, and the runs will be scheduled against the availability of pool and not against a fixed calendar.

# Approvals {#sec-approvals}

This plan takes effect when it has been approved by the functions listed in the approval record at the front of this document. Approval records that the study design in @sec-design, the acceptance criteria in @sec-criteria and the data management provisions in @sec-data are adequate to support the transfer and the viral clearance claim.

A change to the factors, to the ranges in @tbl-params or to the acceptance criteria after approval requires a revision of this plan and re-approval before the affected runs are executed. A change made after the affected runs have been executed will be reported in the report PCR-009 as a deviation from this plan. This revision was issued after the runs of this step, under corrective action CA2 of the investigation INV-001, which amends the step plans with the criteria and the fragment method (@sec-changes).

# Appendix A. Planned screening design matrix {.unnumbered}

@tbl-matrix-scr gives the `{python} n_scr` runs of the screening design in coded and in natural units. The letters are those of @tbl-legend. The coded levels −1, 0 and +1 are the low end, the midpoint and the high end of each range studied in @tbl-params. The executed matrix with its measured responses will appear in the report PCR-009.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_RT = {"factorial": "Factorial", "axial": "Axial", "center": "Centre"}


def _matrix(kind):
    c = D.planned_matrix_df(UO, kind, coded=True)
    n = D.planned_matrix_df(UO, kind, coded=False)
    return pd.DataFrame({"Run type": c["Type"].map(_RT), "Run": c["Run"],
                         "A": c["A"].map(lambda v: g(v).replace("-", "−")),
                         "B": c["B"].map(lambda v: g(v).replace("-", "−")),
                         f"{Vol}, {u_vol}": n[Vol].map(g), f"{Prs}, {u_prs}": n[Prs].map(g)})


T.frame(_matrix("screening"), "Planned screening design, coded and natural settings.",
        "tbl-matrix-scr", merge=["Run type"], align=["l", "r", "r", "r", "R{2.6cm}", "R{2.4cm}"]).show()
```

```{python}
#| output: asis

```

# Appendix B. Planned response-surface design matrix {.unnumbered}

@tbl-matrix-rsm gives the `{python} n_rsm` runs of the response-surface design, in the same coding as Appendix A. The axial runs carry one factor at an edge of its range studied and the other at the midpoint, and the centre point is replicated `{python} cp_rsm` times.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.frame(_matrix("rsm"), "Planned response-surface design, coded and natural settings.",
        "tbl-matrix-rsm", merge=["Run type"], align=["l", "r", "r", "r", "R{2.6cm}", "R{2.4cm}"]).show()
```

The run order within each design is randomized, so the run numbers in these tables identify the design point and not the sequence in which it is run.
